messages:
mike: Heads-up: eu-west-1 queue depth for model gpt-large just spiked to ~42k, admission lag climbing, tails > 800ms for some requests. seeing router 5xxs intermittently.
ani: on it, pulling metrics and p99 traces. any obvious traffic source?
mike: looks like two customers on burst plan + a big batch job from acme-platform. non-prod traffic also mixed in.
jena: we should triage per-model and per-customer. recommend temporary shed for non-prod & best-effort routes, and deprioritize large-batch customers.
jena: proposed admission-control snippet (short):
```yaml
admission:
  default: regular
  rules:
    - match: model == "gpt-large" and region == "eu-west-1"
      action: prioritize
      threshold: 1000
    - match: tag == "non-prod"
      action: reject
      reason: "backlog-shed"
```
ops-bot: alert: metric queue_depth_gpt-large_eu1 > 10k for 6m (pager muted)
sara: can we fallback to gpt-large-q4 in us-west-2? cheaper compute and lower footprint, but cross-region egress cost ~ $0.09/GB -> est $300/hr at current throughput.
linh: cross-region will add ~80-120ms extra latency for EU clients. prefer local shedding before sending traffic west.
ani: quick plan: 1) apply non-prod reject rule 2) cut concurrency for bulk_batch customers 3) enable more aggressive KV prefix cache for gpt-large 4) optional: route low-priority to gpt-large-q4-usw2 if backlog persists
mike: applying non-prod reject and bulk concurrency cap now (`/adm-control apply --policy backlog-shed-eu1`)
mike: pushed changes to adm-control, reducing non-prod and capping bulk concurrency to 4
deploy-bot: rollout finished: adm-control/backlog-shed-eu1 v3 -> prod
ops-bot: metric update: queue_depth_gpt-large_eu1 decreased from 42k -> 9.6k in 7m
sara: nice. cost tradeoff avoided for now. we should still prepare a short-term cross-region plan if spikes continue.
jena: agreed — create runbook item for automatic q4 failover + egress budget guard. also add a post-mortem checklist for customers that hit rejections.
linh: monitoring note: add a p99 latency alert for cross-region fallback so we don't silently degrade SLAs.
ani: collecting trace dumps and sample requests from the offending customers, will DM teams and cc account managers.
mike: thanks all. keeping this thread open for 30m to watch for re-growth. :thumbsup:
